findings.title: Spot summaries omit the higher SPI option

matches.text: | **Spot** | 1 AP | Make an **INT Check** to reveal one eligible **Hidden** enemy combatant. |

**Spot:** A universal action. Choose one **Hidden** enemy within **12"** and **LOS**. **Spot** may choose a **Hidden** combatant despite the targeting restriction in **5.9**. Make an **INT Check** against **12**, with **Disadvantage** if that enemy has **Cover**. On success, that enemy loses **Hidden**. **Spot** does not remove **Invisible** unless a rule says otherwise.

findings.analysis: The action table and glossary require INT alone. The full Spot action permits INT or SPI, whichever is higher; C.4 and C.13 already match it. Under 1.6 the full action governs. A SPI-focused Hero following the stale summaries would lose a legal advantage.
findings.smallest_repair: Copy the higher-of-INT-or-SPI instruction into those two summaries; do not change DC, AP, range, LOS, Cover, or targeting.

findings.title: DEX Pen glossary says damage is unaffected

matches.text: **DEX Pen:** The **DEX** penalty listed by a piece of armour or a shield. It applies to **DEX Checks** and to any rule that uses the **DEX** modifier, and it does not reduce damage. See **7.10**.

Apply a worn armour's **DEX Pen** to the result of the wearer's **DEX Checks**, including **Dodge**, and to any damage total or other value that adds the wearer's **DEX**. If both Chest armour and a shield list a **DEX Pen**, apply only the worse of the two values; **DEX Pen** values do not stack. A worn armour's **Max Speed** caps the combatant's **Speed** while worn.

findings.analysis: The glossary says DEX Pen does not reduce damage, while 7.10 applies it to damage totals and other values that add DEX. Starter profiles in Appendix B follow 7.10. The glossary can produce inflated ranged/Finesse damage.
findings.smallest_repair: Replace the conflicting glossary sentence with the 7.10 scope, including Dodge. Keep the existing armour and shield stacking rules.

findings.title: Impassable Terrain summaries omit the Cover exception

matches.text: | Low walls, barricades, railings, tables, workbenches, platform supports, fallen pillars, broken columns, statue bases, sarcophagi, altars, pedestals | **Impassable Terrain** | - |
| Chasms and pits | **Impassable Terrain** | They provide no **Cover**. |
| **Impassable Terrain** | Cannot be entered, moved through, or ended in. Provides **Cover**. Does not block **LOS**. | **2.9.1** |
**Impassable Terrain:** Terrain that cannot be entered, moved through, or ended in. It provides **Cover**. It does not block **LOS**.

evidence.label: It provides **Cover** unless its terrain entry says otherwise.

matches.text: **Impassable Terrain** cannot be entered or moved through, and a combatant cannot end movement overlapping it. It provides **Cover** unless its terrain entry says otherwise. It does not block **LOS**. A combatant may **Jump** over an **Impassable Terrain** feature if the declared landing point is legal, as described in **4.4.9**; they do not enter the feature.

findings.analysis: The Chapter 4 terrain reference and glossary claim unconditional Cover. RC485 P-02 explicitly made Cover subject to the terrain entry; pits and chasms do not provide it. The authoritative rule already resolves play.
findings.smallest_repair: Add “unless its terrain entry says otherwise” to the two summaries. Preserve P-02 and the distinct terrain types/tags.

findings.title: 9.5 allegiance summary omits same-Group allies

evidence.label: A Monster that is **hostile to all** treats every other combatant as an enemy.

matches.text: - Unless a scenario says otherwise, neutral Monster Groups treat other neutral Monster Groups as allies and every party combatant as an enemy. A Monster that is **hostile to all** treats every other combatant as an enemy.

**Default Monster allegiance:** Unless a scenario says otherwise, all neutral Monster Groups are allied to one another and hostile to every party combatant. They do not target, become **Engaged** with, or wake because of allied Monsters. A Monster or Group that is **hostile to all** treats every other combatant, including Monsters from other Groups, as an enemy. Monsters in the same Group remain allied to one another unless a rule explicitly says otherwise.

findings.analysis: 9.3 preserves allies inside the same Monster Group unless explicitly overridden. 9.5 A omits that exception and can send hostile-to-all Group members against one another. C.8 and the glossary already preserve same-Group allegiance.
findings.smallest_repair: Add the same-Group allied exception to 9.5 A, with “unless a rule explicitly says otherwise”.

findings.title: C.13 AI flow continues after a valid AI Step

matches.text: 4. Evaluate numbered **AI Steps** in ascending order. For a step marked **on d6 N+**, roll **1d6** and require **N** or higher. Resolve the first valid step.

evidence.label: Unless a **Monster** rule explicitly says otherwise, resolving a valid AI Step instruction ends

matches.text: Unless a **Monster** rule explicitly says otherwise, resolving a valid AI Step instruction ends that **Monster's** activation.

findings.smallest_repair: Append the authoritative stop/explicit-continuation instruction to step 4. Do not modify any individual Monster ability.

findings.title: Fifteen enhanced-table values differ from the quality formula

matches.text: #### Tier 1 Enhanced Shield Table (d20)
#### Tier 2 Enhanced Shield Table (d20)
#### Tier 3 Enhanced Shield Table (d20)
#### Tier 5 Enhanced Weapon Table (d20)

evidence.label: Add the listed value adjustment to the base item's cost

matches.text: Add the listed value adjustment to the base item's cost when crafting or purchasing it. After applying all multipliers and flat value adjustments, a finished enhanced weapon, **Chest** armour, or shield has a minimum value set by its quality: **3c** for **Masterwork**, **Silvered**, and **Cold Iron**; **5c** for **Elven**, **Sacred**, and **Palesteel**; and the minimum listed by **Adamantine**. A quality that sets a higher minimum uses that minimum instead. Treasure tables that reference an **Enhanced Weapon Table**, **Enhanced Armour Table**, or **Enhanced Shield Table** grant the finished item shown on that table.

findings.analysis: A complete scan of quality-prefixed enhanced rows reproduces 15 differences from mundane costs and 7.11 multipliers, flat additions, minima, and rounding. Shield differences concern Spiked Targe and Kite Shield; weapon differences concern Repeating Crossbow. Adamantine Steel Scale at 60c is correct because the armour minimum is 60c and is excluded. Importantly, 7.11 grants the finished item printed on a treasure table, so the discrepancies may be intentional treasure valuations rather than arithmetic mistakes. They should not be silently “fixed” during play.
findings.smallest_repair: If one value is intended for purchased/crafted and treasure versions, align only the 15 cells to the existing formula. Exact table replacements are proposed separately from summary/name repairs. Do not change base prices, quality effects, or balance formulas.
findings.uncertainty: The source supplies both a formula and finished-item values, but no justification for these particular exceptions. Author intent on separate treasure valuations is unverified.

findings.title: Two AI charge abilities grant a bonus to an attack they never perform

matches.text: - **Charging Gore (AI Step 1):** Moves their full Speed in a straight line toward the nearest visible enemy; if they end **Engaged**, their **Goring Beak** attack this activation deals an additional **1d8 piercing damage**.

evidence.label: **Run Down (AI Step 1):** Moves their full Speed in a straight line

matches.text: - **Run Down (AI Step 1):** Moves their full Speed in a straight line toward the nearest visible enemy; if they end **Engaged**, their **Bone Jaws** attack this activation rolls its base damage die with **Advantage**.

evidence.label: Remaining AI Steps are not evaluated once a valid AI Step has resolved.

matches.text: A Monster may have one or more numbered **AI Step** abilities (**AI Step 1**, **AI Step 2**, and upward), listed in ascending priority order. Not every Monster has AI Steps; if a Monster has none, skip this part of the script and proceed with standard Monster AI. When a Monster with AI Steps activates, evaluate them in ascending numerical order. If an AI Step is marked **on d6 N+**, roll **1d6** when that step is evaluated; the step is valid only on a result of **N** or higher. An AI Step is otherwise valid only if its trigger is met and every required target, route, attack, and placement is legal. findings.title: Iron-Vein Vault forcing action does not state its successful effect

matches.text: **Breaking a Binding Point (Party B):** A Hero may attack a Binding Point normally, or use **Interact [2 AP]** and pass a **STR Check** to force it. When a Binding Point reaches **0 HP**, it becomes **Broken**. An **Unsealed** or **Sealed** Binding Point can be broken.

**Binding Point States:** Each Binding Point is always in exactly one of three states: **Unsealed**, **Sealed**, or **Broken**. Every Binding Point begins **Unsealed**. Mark each Point's current state with a token beside it. The vault opens when every Binding Point placed after scaling is **Broken** at the same time.

findings.analysis: Interact [2 AP] plus a passed STR Check can “force” a Binding Point, but the only explicit transition to Broken is reaching 0 HP. The text assigns no damage or direct state change to the successful Check. The intended break-open alternative is recognizable, but instant breaking versus HP damage materially changes the opposition’s sealing game.
findings.smallest_repair: State the successful Check result explicitly: e.g. a direct Broken transition or a defined HP effect. Do not supply either without a decision; preserve existing attack and re-sealing rules.

findings.analysis: The Alchemical Golem rolls the type only when an attack has already damaged a target. Type is needed earlier for legal mitigation, Resistance, Immunity, and damage-type critical riders. A target immune to one possible type creates a circular test: whether it was damaged depends on the type that is determined only if damaged.

findings.title: Icebound Court immediate ending prevents its same-round contest

evidence.label: The adventure ends when the Frost Bailiff Magistrate is defeated and either item is escaped with

findings.title: Ritual Chant gives Monsters Advantage on Checks they never roll

matches.text: - **Ritual Chant:** At the start of their activation, allied **Monsters** within **8"** gain **Advantage** on **Checks** to resist Powers and magical item effects until the end of the round.

A **Monster** never makes a Check. A **Monster** has no **STR**, **DEX**, **INT**, or **SPI** score. If a rule would require a **Monster** to make a Check, do not roll it: resolve the effect that would occur on a failed Check against that Monster automatically unless they are **Immune** to it. If a **Power** would require a **Monster** to make such a Check and that **Monster's LVL** is higher than the Level of the Hero casting it, that **Power's Casting Check** is made with **Disadvantage**.

findings.analysis: Mire-Scale Shaman grants allied Monsters Advantage on resistance Checks. 2.3 and 9.1 prohibit Monster Checks and automatically resolve the failed-Check outcome unless immune. Ritual Chant supplies neither a Monster score nor a specific replacement procedure; a modifier alone does not explicitly authorize making a forbidden roll. As written its listed benefit has no effect.
findings.smallest_repair: Choose an explicit defensive effect or an explicit exception with a complete roll procedure. Removing an intentionally inert benefit is also possible. Do not assume Monsters roll d20+0 or gain immunity.

findings.title: Teaching example omits Mara’s automatic armour reduction

findings.title: Teaching example ignores the Dire Wolf’s retained maximum and piercing Critical Hit

evidence.label: Dire Wolf 2 rolls damage with **Advantage** [**1d8 = 3 and 8

matches.text: **Dire Wolf 2** is adjacent to Varek and Dire Wolf 1, so **Pack Tactics** applies. Varek is also **Prone**, but multiple instances of **Advantage** do not stack. Dire Wolf 2 rolls damage with **Advantage** [**1d8 = 3 and 8, keep 8, +1, total 9**]. Varek rolls **AD** [**d6 = 6**], reducing the damage to **3**. Varek falls from **12 HP** to **9 HP**. Because **Bite** dealt damage, Varek makes a **STR Check** [**1d20 = 16, +3 STR, total 19**] and remains **Prone** only from the earlier failed **Check**.
- **Piercing (P):** During mitigation, the attack ignores the target's **AV**, including **AV** generated by **AD**, unless a rule says otherwise.

- **Exploding Dice:** For every retained base damage die that shows its maximum value, roll one additional bonus die of the same type and add it to the total. If a bonus die also shows its maximum value, it explodes again.

findings.analysis: The retained 8 on d8 is a Critical Hit. Bite is piercing, so the printed armour reduction is invalid and at least one exploding bonus d8 must be rolled. With Varek at 12 HP, the minimum is 8+1+1=10 damage, leaving at most 2 HP; a bonus of 3 or more knocks him out. The printed 9 HP, later successful STR Check, Prone state, and subsequent state ledger are not supported.
findings.smallest_repair: Either retain the 8 and supply a complete exploding-die chain, critical rider, damage/KO resolution and dependent ledger, or deliberately change the illustrative base roll and recalculate the attack. Do not weaken Critical Hit rules or assert an unseen bonus roll.

findings.title: Basic Mode combined Traps/Hidden Strongbox variants cannot allocate all tokens

evidence.label: use one or more of the following variants

matches.text: After the first game, use one or more of the following variants to increase replay value without using the full scenario system.

**Traps:** Each **Satchel** and the **Strongbox** is potentially trapped. During setup, prepare **4** face-down tokens for the default scenario: **1** marked **"Trap"** and **3** blank. If the **Advanced Ogre** variant is used, prepare **5** face-down tokens instead: **2** marked **"Trap"** and **3** blank. Place one token under each treasure marker without revealing it.

**Hidden Strongbox:** Place **3 Strongbox** markers along the battlefield midline, each within **6"** of at least one other Strongbox marker. Only one is real. The first time a combatant uses **Interact [1 AP]** while adjacent to a Strongbox marker and not **Engaged**, they make an **INT Check**. On a success, that marker is the real **Strongbox** and may be picked up by the same **Interact**. On a failure, remove that marker as a fake. If **2** fake Strongbox markers have been removed, the last remaining marker is the real **Strongbox**.

findings.analysis: The variants expressly allow combining them. Three Satchels plus three Hidden Strongbox markers require six tokens when Traps says put one under each treasure marker, but it provides four. With Advanced Ogre there are seven markers and five tokens. The text also does not order the fake/real Check against revealing a trap on the same pickup Interact.
findings.smallest_repair: Specify whether fakes receive tokens and how the token count/composition changes, then order Strongbox identification versus trap reveal/pickup. Do not invent additional trap probability.

Its type determines whether it may be entered and its default interaction with **Cover** and **LOS**. Its tags add movement, hazard, or other rules without changing its type.

uncertainties.analysis: Outpost Raid puts Battle Plans and the Commander inside a Blocking Terrain tent. Taken as an entire solid footprint, entry and LOS-based Interact fail. However, 2.9 explicitly separates complex-feature parts/supporting surfaces, defaults floors to Open, and requires pre-play assignment. An enterable tent with Blocking walls may be a legal reading. Similar barrow/dais cases can use distinct floors/upper surfaces and are not automatically contradictions.
uncertainties.next_step: Confirm that the tent has an accessible floor and opening, and distinguish its walls from its interior in setup/diagram. Do not certify an unreachable objective without checking the parts assignment.

evidence.label: Move the Cartographer's Map off the battlefield

uncertainties.title: Move-only Monster steps and “in Reach” wording

matches.text: - **Guard Post (AI Step 1):** Move to remain within **3"** of the nearest allied Monster and attack the nearest enemy in **Reach**. If no ally is on the battlefield, advance on the nearest visible enemy.

- **Hold the Seal (AI Step 1):** Move to the nearest objective marker or allied Undead within **6"** that can be reached, then attack the nearest enemy in **Reach**. If neither exists, advance on the nearest visible enemy.

uncertainties.next_step: Confirm intent or clarify wording to ordinary melee distance; retain default distance and end-after-step behaviour pending that decision.

uncertainties.title: Teaching aids: two-square footprint and objective setup order

evidence.label: A Ranger targets a two-square Monster in Grid Mode.

matches.text: *A Ranger targets a two-square Monster in Grid Mode. Under **2.6**, test source-square and target-square pairs using one pair for range, **LOS**, and **Cover**. One pair has a sight line that touches the corner of a **Cover Terrain** square but does not pass through that square's interior and crosses no **Blocking Terrain**. That pair has **LOS**, and the touched terrain grants **Cover**. If another legal pair gives the target less Cover, use that pair instead; if Cover is tied, use the shortest range. If every possible pair is blocked by **Blocking Terrain**, a solid floor/roof/platform, or the interior of an intervening **Cover Terrain** square as described in **2.7.2**, the Ranger has no **LOS**.*
#### 10.5.2 Solo and Cooperative Setup Checklist

uncertainties.analysis: C.12’s “two-square Monster” does not match standard 1×1, 2×2 or 3×3 footprints unless it means two squares wide. Separately, solo setup deploys Monsters before placing objectives/hazards although some deployments depend on those positions. Planning the positions in advance may satisfy the latter without a rules change.
uncertainties.next_step: Use an explicit standard footprint in the example if desired; clarify planning/deployment dependencies without treating the appendix as an override or inventing a new setup phase.

Solo conversion/extraction continues past competitive ending conditions where 10.5.5 explicitly says so.

The global six-Group limit rejects a seventh placement event. A setup with five Random Groups plus multiple scenario Groups may omit a later Group, but is not allowed to place seven. The allocation may merit balance review; no new cap or merging rule is needed to resolve legality.
Boss Relentless activations, their per-round cap, and lack of ordinary Monster Phase activation are explicit; start-of-Monster-Phase effects remain applicable.

Throwing Knives always use one base die; Martial Supremacy and other die increases do not override the explicit exception.
Scenario CV/role deviations are deliberately allowed in 10.6.4; no automatic Monster repricing is justified.
Historical accounts of the Fall are deliberately competing/unreliable. No external canon was used to invent lore corrections.
